study: Noh et al. (2026), BMC Public Health
applicability: Limited to prevalent-status classification; not prospective risk prediction
rationale: Clear BRFSS 2023/_MICHD framing, held-out evaluation, train-only preprocessing and explicit proxy-exclusion sensitivity; ML not fully complex-survey weighted and model uses broad predictors.
caveat: Single-reviewer desk appraisal; not a formal author or independent PROBAST+AI rating.

study: Kung et al. (2026), International Journal of Medical Sciences
access_level: Publisher indexed page/search result only; direct full-text page retrieval failed
applicability: Methodological analogue for annual-BRFSS temporal validation; not direct MI/CHD comparator
overall_provisional: Insufficient access for a meaningful domain-level rating
rationale: The accessible publisher result confirms BRFSS 2023 development and frozen BRFSS 2024 temporal evaluation without refitting/retuning/threshold adjustment. Full methods/results were not independently extracted, so PROBAST+AI domain ratings would be speculative.
caveat: Do not infer low or high risk of bias from the abstract/indexed result; obtain full text before a formal appraisal.

study: Chavda & Hyun (2024), Journal of Emerging Investigators
applicability: Survey-history classification; no clinical deployment validation
rationale: Large BRFSS 2022 sample, held-out 10% and stratified five-fold CV; however sample composition is skewed, outcome is self-reported, calibration and complex-survey weighting were not reported in examined methods, and exact _MICHD code equivalence was not confirmed.
caveat: Single-reviewer desk appraisal; methods appear adequate for exploratory classification but do not establish clinical utility.

study: Imani et al. (2026), American Heart Journal Plus
access_level: Accessible abstract and article text reviewed
applicability: Limited to cross-sectional survey classification; no external clinical validation identified
rationale: Accessible article contains a sample-count mismatch and conflicting abstract versus table accuracy values; complete-case restriction and no complex-survey design evaluation also limit interpretation.
caveat: Do not infer misconduct or a confirmed implementation error; reconcile with authors/code/supplement before relying on the disputed metrics.

access_level: Full text methods/results/limitations reviewed; code not audited
applicability: Not established outside the derived BRFSS dataset
overall_provisional: High concern if the described resampling order reflects execution
rationale: The methods describe SMOTE and dataset expansion before the train/validation/test split section and then describe a smaller subsample. This sequence creates a possible leakage/reproducibility concern; the reported implementation was not independently reproduced.
caveat: The concern is conditional and text-based, not a confirmed error; inspect code/supplement or seek clarification.

study: Wu et al. (2026), Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
applicability: Cross-survey external validation, but target alignment to _MICHD is unconfirmed
rationale: BRFSS internal split and NHANES external evaluation are reported, but the full methods, exact outcome mapping, calibration, and complex-survey handling were not established from the accessible abstract.
caveat: Abstract-only appraisal cannot support a confident domain-level rating.

applicability: Cross-dataset CHD classification with heterogeneous populations/outcomes
rationale: Uses BRFSS 2015 with Framingham and Z-Alizadeh Sani validation datasets; heterogeneous target definitions and populations limit comparability to current _MICHD annual-sample design.
caveat: Appraisal is contextual; not a direct same-outcome/same-design benchmark.

study: Current project: BRFSS 2023 development / BRFSS 2025 frozen evaluation
access_level: Repository documents, result tables and provenance reviewed
applicability: Research-only prevalent-status classification; not a clinical tool or future-risk model
rationale: Strengths include locked 2023 test, frozen 2025 application, explicit outcome-overlap exclusion, calibration and robustness analyses. Concerns include unresolved local/current CDC file fingerprint/column-count discrepancy, cross-sectional self-report, survey-weighted point estimates without design-based CIs, and subgroup variability.
caveat: Self-appraisal is not independent validation or a formal PROBAST+AI certification; no model results were changed in Phase 2.
